2 Samuel 18:19: Ahimaaz son of Zadok said, “Let me run and bring the king good news: the Lord has vindicated him against the hand of his enemies.”

2 Samuel 18:21: Joab said to Cushi, “Go, report to the king everything you have seen.” Cushi bowed to Joab and went out.
2 Samuel 18:22: Ahimaaz son of Zadok spoke again to Joab: “Let me too run after Cushi.” Joab said, “Why are you running, my son? Come here. There is no news that will benefit you by going.”
2 Samuel 18:23: He said, “What if I do run?” Joab told him, “Run.” Ahimaaz ran by the road of Kechar and overtook Cushi.
2 Samuel 18:24: David was sitting between the two gates. The watchman went up to the gate roof by the wall, raised his eyes, and saw a man running alone before him.
2 Samuel 18:25: The watchman called out and told the king. The king said, “If he is alone, there is good news in his mouth.” The man kept coming nearer.
2 Samuel 18:26: The watchman saw another man running. He called out by the gate, “There is another man running alone.” The king said, “He too brings good news.”
2 Samuel 18:27: The watchman said, “I recognize the first man’s running: it is like Ahimaaz son of Zadok’s.” The king said, “He is a good man; he comes with good news.”
2 Samuel 18:28: Ahimaaz called to the king, “Peace!” He bowed to the king with his face to the ground and said, “Blessed is the Lord your God, who has shut out the men who hated their hand against my lord the king.”
2 Samuel 18:29: The king asked, “Is the young man Absalom well?” Ahimaaz said, “I saw a great crowd when Joab sent the king’s servant and your servant, but I did not know what was there.”
2 Samuel 18:30: The king said, “Turn aside and stand here.” He turned aside and stood.
2 Samuel 18:31: Then Cushi arrived and said to the king, “Let my lord the king receive good news: the Lord has vindicated you today against the hand of all who rose against you.”
2 Samuel 18:32: The king asked Cushi, “Is the young man Absalom well?” Cushi said, “May the enemies of my lord the king, and all who rose against him to do harm, be like that young man.”
